generatedProse.concept-context: Across subjects, exams come in several forms, and each asks for something different. A multiple-choice exam might test your recall of key facts or methods. A longer written exam asks you to argue a case and weigh the evidence. A short-answer exam wants precise definitions. Knowing which type you face tells you what good revision looks like.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two students who are told their module has a written essay exam, and both begin preparing.

Student A revises as for any test, memorising definitions and facts, ready to write them down. They know a great deal of detail, but they have not practised building an argument, which is what an essay exam asks for.

Student B first asks what this type of exam is testing. An essay exam wants a reasoned argument, so they practise planning answers, weighing points, and writing to time. They memorise fewer isolated facts, but they can use what they know to make a case.

Both revised hard. Only Student B matched the preparation to what an essay exam demands.
generatedProse.summary: Exams come in several forms: multiple-choice exams test recall, essay exams want a reasoned argument, short-answer exams reward precise explanation, and others test applying a method. You can now identify the main types and see why the type you face should shape your revision. The next lesson turns to why a revision strategy matters.

check.body: In the worked example, why was Student B's preparation better suited to an essay exam?

items.text: They practised building and writing a reasoned argument, weighing points, which is what an essay exam asks for.
They memorised more definitions and facts than Student A.
They revised for more hours than Student A.
They started revising the night before the exam.

feedback.correct: That's right. Practising a reasoned argument matched what an essay exam demands.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for the preparation that fits what an essay exam is actually asking for.
feedback.incorrectFinal: An essay exam asks for a reasoned argument, and Student B practised exactly that. Memorising more, or longer hours, does not match the task.
